exposure: maternal serum free beta human chorionic gonadotropin (free b-hCG) levels (elevated vs. normal)
cohort: The study included 22,745 women with singleton pregnancies who delivered at Hangzhou Women's Hospital between January 2018 and December 2020 and underwent second-trimester free b-hCG screening.
finding: Elevated maternal serum free b-hCG levels in the second trimester are associated with increased risks of polyhydramnios, preeclampsia, hyperlipidemia, intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), and having female infants.
